transcript.text: Thank you both for joining me. As part of our standard facilities-and-curriculum pre-approval review, I need to hear from you before I can finalize my decision on the courtyard science learning garden proposal. The current plan calls for planting six species directly in the existing soil, starting in September, with three science lessons held in the garden. Before I approve the conversion and its operating plan, I need each of you to report anything that should be included or flagged — whether it's a facilities concern, a curriculum concern, or anything else you think I need to know. What are you seeing?

transcript.text: Dr. Morgan, I need to flag a serious facilities concern. I received a soil laboratory report yesterday that found lead at 185 parts per million in the courtyard soil. That's above our district's 100-parts-per-million threshold. District procedure requires us to remove the top 8 inches of soil and replace it with certified clean soil before students can use the garden. This report is still in my facilities folder awaiting weekly review and has not yet been added to the project proposal, so it wasn't reflected in the current plan.

transcript.text: Dr. Morgan, I need to raise a critical curriculum concern. The science department's executed garden-learning grant, which I received the terms for just this week, requires the project to include exactly 10 native plant species — not the six currently in the proposal. It also requires exactly 6 science lessons in the garden by November 1, 2026 — not the three currently planned. Finally, it requires supervised maintenance to be scheduled on Tuesdays and Thursdays at 2:30 p.m. The proposal was drafted before the grant award was finalized, so none of these requirements are reflected in the current plan. We need to revise the proposal to meet these grant terms before approval.
